proposals.before: When Emperor Xuanzong died and Emperor Suzong was gravely ill, an edict appointed Jinqing acting chief mourner; he firmly declined, saying: "The late emperor's testamentary edict states that the emperor shall hold court after three days; consulting ancestral precedent, there is no provision for a chief mourner; following the testamentary edict, he should attend court.
proposals.after: When Emperor Xuanzong died and Emperor Suzong was gravely ill, an edict appointed Jinqing acting chief minister (zhongzai); he firmly declined, saying: "The late emperor's testamentary edict states that the emperor shall hold court after three days; consulting ancestral precedent, there is no provision for a chief minister; following the testamentary edict, he should attend court.
proposals.reason: 冢宰 is the classical chief-minister office, confirmed by 攝政 in s0056; it is not chief mourner.

proposals.before: When Emperor Xuanzong died and Emperor Suzong was gravely ill, an edict appointed Jinqing acting chief mourner; he firmly declined, saying: "The late Emperor's testamentary edict states that the Emperor shall hold court after three days; consulting the precedents of our ancestors, there is no provision for a chief mourner; following the testamentary edict, he should attend court.
proposals.after: When Emperor Xuanzong died and Emperor Suzong was gravely ill, an edict appointed Jinqing acting chief minister (zhongzai); he firmly declined, saying: "The late Emperor's testamentary edict states that the Emperor shall hold court after three days; consulting the precedents of our ancestors, there is no provision for a chief minister; following the testamentary edict, he should attend court.
proposals.reason: Same 冢宰 mistranslation as in the idiomatic field.

proposals.before: Several days later Emperor Daizong ascended; again he was ordered to act as chief mourner, and only after firmly declining was he released from the duty.
proposals.after: Several days later Emperor Daizong ascended; again he was ordered to act as chief minister (zhongzai), and only after firmly declining was he released from the duty.
proposals.reason: Repeats the 冢宰 mistranslation; the office is acting chief minister.

proposals.before: Several days later Emperor Daizong ascended; again he was ordered to act as chief mourner, and only after firmly declining was he released from the duty.
proposals.after: Several days later Emperor Daizong ascended; again he was ordered to act as chief minister (zhongzai), and only after firmly declining was he released from the duty.
proposals.reason: Same 冢宰 mistranslation as the idiomatic field.

proposals.before: Mian had studied the classics from youth, yet he was sharp and keen and decisive in affairs; everyone regarded him as competent in office, and Hong relied on him greatly.
proposals.after: Mian had little scholarly learning, yet he was sharp and keen and decisive in affairs; everyone regarded him as competent in office, and Hong relied on him greatly.
proposals.reason: The contrast 少學術…然 means scant learning, not study from youth.

proposals.before: Mian studied the arts from youth, yet was sharp and keen, decisive in affairs; the multitude presented him as competent in office, and Hong greatly relied on him.
proposals.after: Mian had scant scholarship, yet was sharp and keen, decisive in affairs; the multitude presented him as competent in office, and Hong greatly relied on him.
proposals.reason: 少學術 with 然 marks lack of learning rather than youthful study.

proposals.before: Xuan violated the law and was demoted to prefect of Shizhou, then transferred to Lizhou.
proposals.after: Xuan violated the law, and Mian was implicated and demoted to prefect of Shizhou, then transferred to Lizhou.
proposals.reason: 坐降 in this biography marks the subject's implicated demotion, not Liu Xuan's.

proposals.before: Xuan violated the law and, on that account, was demoted to prefect of Shizhou and moved to Lizhou.
proposals.after: Xuan violated the law, and on that account Mian was demoted to prefect of Shizhou and moved to Lizhou.
proposals.reason: 坐降 refers to Pei Mian as the biographical subject.

proposals.before: At that time Yuan Zai held power; Mian had long ago been selected and promoted by him; Zai was grateful and also took advantage of his feeble illness—and moreover humbled himself before Zai—so Mian was appointed minister of the left and grand councillor of the Secretariat and Chancellery.
proposals.after: At that time Yuan Zai held power; Mian had long ago selected and promoted him; Zai was grateful and also took advantage of Mian's feeble illness—and that Mian would stand below him—so Mian was appointed minister of the left and grand councillor of the Secretariat and Chancellery.
proposals.reason: 冕早所甄引 means Mian had earlier selected Yuan Zai, matching 載德之.

proposals.before: At that time Yuan Zai held state affairs; Mian had long ago been selected and promoted by him; Zai was grateful to him and also coveted his feeble illness—and moreover humbled himself—so Mian was appointed Minister of the Left and Grand Councillor of the Secretariat and Chancellery.
proposals.after: At that time Yuan Zai held state affairs; Mian had long ago selected and promoted him; Zai was grateful to him and also coveted his feeble illness—and that Mian would stand below him—so Mian was appointed Minister of the Left and Grand Councillor of the Secretariat and Chancellery.
proposals.reason: 所甄引 has Mian as selector of Yuan Zai, not the reverse.

proposals.before: When his years had grown long he first entered office through yin privilege as an official household and was appointed deputy of Xingning Mausoleum, then transferred to aide in the Court of Judicial Review.
proposals.after: When his years had grown long he first entered office through the yin privilege of an official family as deputy of Xingning Mausoleum, then transferred to aide in the Court of Judicial Review.
proposals.reason: 仕家推蔭 means appointment through an official family's hereditary privilege, not that he served 'as an official household'.

proposals.before: Once a clansman by marriage, deranged by illness, accused him of plotting rebellion; the emperor recognized the absurdity and took no notice.
proposals.after: Once a junior clansman, deranged by illness, accused him of plotting rebellion; the emperor recognized the absurdity and took no notice.
proposals.reason: 族子 is a junior agnatic kinsman, not a relative by marriage.

proposals.before: Once a clansman by marriage, sick with mania, reported that Zunqing was plotting rebellion; the Emperor recognized the absurdity and set it aside without inquiry.
proposals.after: Once a junior clansman, sick with mania, reported that Zunqing was plotting rebellion; the Emperor recognized the absurdity and set it aside without inquiry.
proposals.reason: 族子 does not mean 'clansman by marriage'.

proposals.before: When Du Shenquan held Hedong he memorialized that Shu enter his staff; he was twice promoted to magistrate of Lantian.
proposals.after: When Du Shenquan held Hezhong he memorialized that Shu enter his staff; he was twice promoted to lieutenant of Lantian.
proposals.reason: Chinese 河中 is Hezhong; 藍田尉 is a county lieutenant, but the Hedong error is the clear semantic fault.
